paper.title: ROCKET: Exceptionally Fast and Accurate Time Series Classification Using Random Convolutional Kernels
paper.note: Not committed; pass 02_ROCKET.pdf as the second argument. Its SHA-256 must match.

claim.method: ROCKET with 10,000 random convolutional kernels and RidgeClassifierCV

repository.why: The official repository linked by the paper; its reproduction script runs ROCKET over the UCR archive and its committed results contain the ECG200 10-run mean and population standard deviation.

notes: The repository does not pin versions. These versions have Python 3.11 binary wheels and preserve RidgeClassifierCV(normalize=True), which newer scikit-learn releases remove.
The tolerance is sealed before execution. It is 0.0053: the rounded 95% two-sample mean allowance t(9,0.975) × 0.00516398 × sqrt(1/10 + 1/10), using the official repository's 10-run population SD.

dataset.license: UCR/UEA archive terms; dataset page does not state a separate license

expected.why: A project-owned adapter caps the result at partially_reproduced. The real run may honestly be not_reproduced if its independently sampled 10-run mean falls outside the pre-registered statistical tolerance.

caveats: ROCKET is intentionally stochastic; exact equality with the paper is neither required nor expected.
The official repository records ECG200 mean 0.906 and population SD 0.00516398 for 10 runs; the paper prints the mean in Table 1.
The one-dataset adapter is project-owned because the upstream script crashes on a one-row dataset-name file; this caps the status at partially_reproduced.

paperAnalyst.summary: Table 1 reports ROCKET mean test accuracy 0.9060 on the fixed UCR ECG200 split; the method uses 10,000 random kernels and the experiments use 10 runs.

claim.method: ROCKET with 10,000 random convolutional kernels and RidgeClassifierCV
claim.split: the fixed UCR train/test split (100 train, 100 test)
claim.preprocessing: the UCR ECG200 text-format split is loaded directly; ROCKET creates 10,000 random convolutional kernels per run
claim.seedPolicy: 10 independent runs with different random kernels; no fixed seeds are stated

repositoryAnalyst.summary: code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py loads fixed UCR text splits, generates 10,000 random kernels per run, fits RidgeClassifierCV, and writes mean accuracy and population standard deviation.

entrypoints.why: the official UCR experiment reproduction script

repositoryAnalyst.runInstructions: Run reproduce_experiments_ucr.py with the UCR text-format parent directory, a dataset-name file, 10 runs, and 10,000 kernels.
